context: Tests whether the agent adds machine-readable health and request signals, implements collision-free worktree startup with bounded readiness and cleanup, and handles the explicitly required ignored local config without prescribing one port-allocation algorithm.

checklist.name: Health response has status field
checklist.description: The /health endpoint returns a JSON object containing a 'status' key (e.g., {"status": "ok", ...})

checklist.name: Health response is operationally useful
checklist.description: The health response includes enough stable machine-readable context to distinguish ready from unavailable; version, uptime, dependency readiness, or an equivalent useful signal is accepted

checklist.name: Structured JSON request logging
checklist.description: app.py emits a structured JSON log line for each request (not plain print statements) — containing at minimum method, path, and status fields

checklist.name: Concurrent port allocation is collision-free
checklist.description: worktree-start.sh obtains or computes an isolated port per worktree or task using a runner assignment, deterministic allocation, ephemeral-port protocol, or equivalent collision-resistant mechanism

checklist.name: No hardcoded port 5000
checklist.description: worktree-start.sh does NOT use a hardcoded port 5000 (or any other fixed port number)

checklist.name: Background app start in worktree-start.sh
checklist.description: worktree-start.sh starts the Flask application in the background (using & or equivalent)

checklist.name: Bounded readiness wait in worktree-start.sh
checklist.description: worktree-start.sh waits for the health endpoint until a finite attempt or wall-clock deadline before declaring success, without relying on one fixed iteration count

checklist.name: Non-zero exit on boot failure
checklist.description: worktree-start.sh exits with a non-zero status if the app fails to start within the polling period

checklist.name: teardown.sh stops service
checklist.description: teardown.sh stops the Flask service (kills the process by PID or uses a stop command)

checklist.name: Port collision rationale documented
checklist.description: observability-notes.md explains how the chosen resource-allocation contract prevents collisions between concurrent worktrees and who owns that allocation

checklist.name: .worktreeinclude exists
checklist.description: The solution creates a .worktreeinclude file at the repository root

checklist.name: .worktreeinclude is narrow
checklist.description: .worktreeinclude includes .env.local or the required local config path, and does not use broad patterns such as *, .env*, secrets/, node_modules/, or build/cache directories

checklist.name: .gitignore matches worktree include
checklist.description: .gitignore ignores the same local config file that .worktreeinclude includes, so the file is eligible for managed Codex or Claude worktree copying

checklist.name: Worktree include rationale documented
checklist.description: observability-notes.md explains that managed Codex or Claude worktrees copy only matching gitignored files from .worktreeinclude, and that manual worktrees/hooks need their own copy path

checklist.name: Dev environment observability
checklist.description: observability-notes.md or app.py adds observability to the development/local environment (not just describing it as a production concern)
